cues: The passive of every tense follows the same logic: be carries the tense, and the past participle never changes.
He writes: a letter is written.
He is writing: a letter is being written.
He has written: has been written.
He was writing: was being written.
He had written: had been written.
He will write: will be written.
He must write: must be written.
And he must have written: it must have been written.
text: The passive of every tense follows the same logic: be carries the tense, and the past participle never changes. He writes: a letter is written. He is writing: a letter is being written. He has written: has been written. He wrote: was written. He was writing: was being written. He had written: had been written. He will write: will be written. He must write: must be written. And he must have written: it must have been written.
